evals.prompt: Design a small three.js ambient world where every GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode session is an inhabitant and each repository owns a territory. Give me the implementation architecture and the session-state-to-behaviour mapping before writing code.
evals.expected_output: A concrete, harness-agnostic design covering the reader/adapter, mapper, renderer, and thin server; a single ordered state function; stable repository layout; and the key interaction and rendering constraints.
expectations: The response explicitly includes GitHub Copilot CLI alongside Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
The architecture separates a session reader, world-state mapper, renderer, and thin server.
The state mapping uses ordered precedence and includes errored, working, merged/finished, waiting, dormant, and ordinary states.
The layout is described as stable across polls and persisted across reloads.

evals.prompt: I need to render 300 animated astronaut-like agents in a three.js dashboard. The current prototype creates one SkinnedMesh and Skeleton per session and drops frames. Explain the redesign and the shader/rendering details that must not be missed.
evals.expected_output: A performance-focused redesign that bakes clips into a bone-matrix texture, renders the crowd through one InstancedMesh, skins in the vertex shader before instance transforms, and preserves the related attachment, loop, quality, and post-processing invariants.
expectations: The response recommends animation-texture/bone-matrix baking instead of one CPU skeleton per agent.
The response recommends one instanced crowd draw and says skinning must happen before the per-instance transform such as instanceMatrix.
The response warns that non-looping clips must be sampled just short of their duration so their final pose holds.
The response covers render scale separate from device pixel ratio and an adaptive governor that changes gradually rather than per frame.
The response says depth-based tilt-shift must use the depth written by the current post-processing buffer and that disabling effects should dispose render targets.

evals.prompt: Add a new local harness adapter for a coding-agent CLI to an existing Bot Crossing-style JavaScript app. The adapter should scan session files, open a session when possible, and archive it when the harness supports archiving. What should the adapter contract and safety checklist be?
evals.expected_output: A minimal adapter contract and checklist that keeps harness-specific formats isolated, reads bounded transcript heads, validates opaque ids and paths, uses argument arrays for openers, defaults to read-only, and performs only a verified atomic archive-field write.
expectations: The response keeps adapter-specific knowledge in one module and says the scanner, API, and renderer should not need harness-specific changes.
The response requires stable globally unique thread ids and an opaque serializable ref.
The response requires bounded head reads, mtime caching, malformed-record tolerance, and process/activity checks where relevant.
The response requires read-only behavior by default, verification of the record id, and a temp-file-plus-rename atomic write for the single archive flag.
The response requires validated ids and paths plus argument arrays rather than shell command strings.
